Compares; secondary: Evaluates — compares native vs foreign specifications across agents and rewrite, compression and RAG ingestion strategies; also evaluates Stage 1 feasibility of a specification-first Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration pipeline

Stage 1: authors' specification-first (Code-Text-Code) migration pipeline with an agent loop and MCP tools, no version. Stage 2: SDD environments, no versions: Amazon Kiro; GitHub Spec Kit + GitHub Copilot; Google Antigravity + Gemini; Claude Code and Cursor (initial single-agent stage only). Ingestion strategies: direct, rewrite, compression/summarisation, retrieval-augmented (RAG)

Stage 1: per-database-object intermediate specification (behaviour, identifiers, flow, conditions, dependencies, side effects, intent) from which PostgreSQL code is derived. Stage 2: each environment's native specification (Kiro ~1,597 lines; Gemini ~193 lines); artefact structure per tool not described

Stage 1: preprocess and decompose source SQL into objects -> agent generates specification -> derives PostgreSQL code (iterative tool loop until finish/iteration limit). Task: same functional request (deterministic Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration utility) to each environment; evaluation on 1,802 Oracle scripts with reference PostgreSQL. Configurations: native spec per agent (Kiro, Copilot/Spec Kit, Gemini/Antigravity; Claude Code and Cursor only in initial single-agent), 3 x 3 origin x implementer matrix with 7 of 9 cells evaluated (3 native + 4 of 6 foreign transfers; Copilot-origin spec -> Kiro and -> Gemini not evaluated), and rewrite/compression/RAG for Kiro-origin specs (compression only for Copilot). Baseline: native-specification condition, rerun before cross-agent stage. Held constant: functional request, dataset, metrics; models, prompts, versions, operator Not stated. Acceptance tests: reference scripts and runnability (lower bound). Repetitions: single runs, except Gemini<-Kiro repeated once. Human intervention: human review in native workflow; not described for transfers. Stage 1 separate (1,006 files, two models)

Spec size does not predict quality (Kiro largest ~1,597 lines, not best). Transfer is asymmetric and agent-dependent: Gemini degrades strongly with Kiro spec (replicated: F1 0.035, SQL validity 2.33%, AST sim 0.015, vs native 0.73/45.54%/0.69); Copilot stable or improved with foreign specs (Gemini spec: SQL validity 63% vs native 43.51%). Rewrite improved Gemini (SQL 43.62%) but hurt Copilot (14.09%); compression no universal benefit; RAG not best on every metric but the only strategy on both per-agent Pareto frontiers (SQL validity x AST similarity). No significance testing

Distinguished agents and strategies on several metrics, but runnability near 0-2% for most configurations limits discrimination on operational quality. Repeatability: only one configuration replicated; authors note nondeterminism and interpret single runs cautiously. Limitations stated: conclusions restricted to observed agents, specs, strategies, dataset and metrics; runnability is a lower bound (empty DB with stubs); native baseline not originally designed as a controlled baseline; pricing limited agents

Results do not support that foreign specs are inherently worse; current experiments insufficient to claim RAG universally optimal; procedural/dependency-sensitive objects remain difficult. Future work: specification portability, structured (block-based) specification representations, agent-specific adaptation views, dependency-aware retrieval for multi-agent SDD

Inconsistencies: Table III first-run Gemini<-Kiro F1 0.68 (SQL validity 0) vs replicated F1 0.035, described as 'the same qualitative failure pattern'; the values 13.15 (EM) and 43.51 (SQL validity) recur across unrelated configurations: Copilot native (13.15/43.51), Kiro<-Gemini (13.15/43.51), Gemini rewrite of Kiro spec (EM 13.15, Table V) and Copilot RAG of Kiro spec (SQL 43.51, Table VII), which suggests copy errors; Table II 'tuned' single-agent values differ widely from Table I native baselines (e.g. Copilot runnable 17.48% vs 0%), tuning not explained; runnable 'Not implemented' for Copilot<-Gemini. Tables extracted with jumbled columns, mapping done from row order (check Tables I-VII). Figures 4-5 (Pareto) not in text. Models used by Kiro/Copilot/Gemini/Claude Code/Cursor not stated. No data/code availability stated. No pre-registration. Languages: PL/SQL, PostgreSQL SQL; utility language Not stated. Authors' prior work (Code-Text-Code, token optimisation) underlies Stage 1
